patches.name: Bypass Emulator Detection
patches.description:
Hides emulator traces by spoofing Build info and related checks so apps cannot detect an emulator.

Compatibility: PairIP Bypass and other server-side integrity systems can still reject a
device when entitlement is bound to genuine device signals, package identity, or attestation.
Combining spoofing with those patches is app-specific and cannot safely bypass remote checks.

Credits: Nai64Patches from Nai64.

patches.name: Control App Ads Patch (Experimental, Enhanced)
patches.description:
A merged ad-control patch based on Nai64's No Ads and Ads Free Rewards patches, plus
literal-host blocking inspired by Entree and Adobo. Block common ad formats, choose the
SDKs to target, optionally grant ad rewards without an ad, and redirect matching literal
ad/tracker hosts embedded in the APK.

Host filters are built-in domain sets, not downloaded subscriptions. They only affect
hosts stored as literal strings by the app; they cannot block dynamically generated hosts,
encrypted traffic, or requests made entirely inside Google Play services.

Compatibility: when combined with Disable Forced Online Checks, keep that patch's “Exclude
ad SDK and networking code” option enabled; otherwise blocked ad hosts may be treated as
online and retried. PairIP Firebase cleanup/removal can disable Firebase-backed reward,
sign-in, billing, and attribution flows, which this patch cannot restore.

Credits: Nai64Patches from Nai64; host-blocking approach inspired by Entree and Adobo.

patches.name: Custom App Display Patch (Experimental, Enhanced)
patches.description:
Configure display compatibility for an APK: aspect-ratio scaling, a Unity window-resolution
override, preferred refresh rate, Unity renderer preference, ANGLE preference, and game
category hints. Android and the app remain in control and can ignore any request.

Resolution and renderer overrides currently target Unity activities. Scaling removes Android
aspect-ratio restrictions where present; it cannot universally rescale every game engine.

Custom App Resolution and game-optimization inspiration: Nai64Patches from Nai64.
Frame-rate, graphics-driver, ANGLE, and aspect-ratio controls are UniPatches work.

options.title: Display scaling > Mode
options.description: Default preserves the app's behavior. Remove aspect restrictions lets Android use more screen space without forcing a stretch. Stretch to screen also requests resizable activities; engines may still keep their own letterboxing.

options.title: Resolution override > Enable
options.description: Request this window size for supported Unity activities. Disabled by default. Fullscreen games and Android window policy may override it.

options.title: Resolution override > Width (px)
options.description: Requested horizontal window size in pixels when Resolution override is enabled. Default: 1920.

options.title: Resolution override > Height (px)
options.description: Requested vertical window size in pixels when Resolution override is enabled. Default: 1080. Swap width and height for portrait content.

options.title: Frame rate > Enable FPS preference
options.description: Request a preferred display refresh rate for every Activity window in the APK. This cannot exceed the display, bypass a game FPS cap, or override battery/thermal policy.

options.title: Frame rate > Target FPS
options.description: Preferred display refresh rate used when Enable FPS preference is on. Default: 60 FPS.

options.title: Graphics > API preference
options.description: Decided by app makes no renderer change. OpenGL ES and Vulkan add a Unity launch argument only when a supported Unity player activity exists. ANGLE adds Android's official GLES-driver preference metadata on supported devices.

options.title: Game mode > Optimization preference
options.description: Decided by app makes no change. Mark as game adds Android's game app-category hint, which may let the device offer its own game optimizations. It cannot force an OEM Game Mode on or off.

patches.name: Custom App Output Patch (Experimental, Enhanced)
patches.description:
Customize an APK's install identity and launcher presentation in one patch. Clone mode can
install a side-by-side copy, while name, icon, hide-icon, and target-SDK options are
independent. This cannot preserve original-app data when a package or signing identity
changes. Clone mode rewrites supported manifest identifiers only; it does not rewrite
bytecode strings, explicit process names, task affinities, or arbitrary SDK configuration.
A clone has a new Android package identity and normally a new signing identity: package- or
certificate-bound OAuth, Firebase, Google Play Games, billing, deep links, and server
licenses may therefore not work and cannot be repaired safely by this patch. If PairIP
Bypass is also enabled, server/package-bound PairIP enforcement can still reject the clone.

Inspired by Nai64Patches from Nai64: Clone, Custom App Icon, Hide App Icon, and target
SDK customization patches.

options.title: Clone > Enable clone
options.description: Create a side-by-side install by changing the manifest package name. Disabled by default. This does not bypass app signatures or preserve original-app data. Package/certificate-bound OAuth, Firebase, Google Play Games, billing, deep links, and server licenses may stop working; PairIP cannot reliably bypass server package checks on a clone.

options.title: Clone > Package name mode
options.description: Append adds a suffix to the original package, such as com.example.app.u. Complete replace uses the Package name override exactly as entered.

options.title: Clone > Append package suffix
options.description: Suffix used by Append mode. Use one or more lowercase package segments, for example .u, .clone, or .patched.test. A leading dot is added automatically when omitted.

options.title: Clone > Package name override
options.description: Complete replacement package name used only in Complete replace mode, for example com.example.mycopy. Leave empty when using Append mode.

options.title: Clone > Compatibility > Rewrite provider authorities
options.description: Update ContentProvider authorities that begin with the original package. This avoids common side-by-side install conflicts.

options.title: Clone > Compatibility > Rewrite custom permissions
options.description: Update app-defined permission names and matching uses-permission entries that begin with the original package.

options.title: Clone > Compatibility > Preserve relative components
options.description: Expand relative Activity, Service, Receiver, Provider, and alias class names to the original package before cloning. This prevents Android from searching for classes in the new package.

options.title: Custom App Name > Launcher name
options.description: Name shown in the home launcher. It updates the application label and launcher activities or aliases. Leave empty to keep the original name.

options.title: App Icon > Hide launcher icon
options.description: Replace launcher icons with a transparent drawable. The app remains installed and launchable, but its launcher entry appears blank. This takes priority over Custom app icon.

options.title: Custom App Icon > Enable custom icon
options.description: Replace the application and all Activity or Activity-alias icon attributes with your supplied image. Ignored when Hide launcher icon is enabled.

options.title: Custom App Icon > Local image
options.description: Local PNG, JPG, JPEG, or WebP file. A square image with transparent padding is recommended. This source takes priority over String Handler.

options.title: Custom App Icon > String Handler
options.description: Fallback icon source when Local image is empty: a raw Base64 image string, data:image/...;base64,..., or an HTTPS image URL. Example Base64 input: <base64 string here>. You can encode an image at https://base64.guru/converter/encode/image.

options.title: Compatibility > Target SDK > Override target SDK
options.description: Write a targetSdkVersion into the manifest. Enable only when you need to address an installer compatibility issue, because changing it can alter Android behavior.

options.title: Compatibility > Target SDK > Version
options.description: Target SDK used when Override target SDK is enabled. Common current values are 34 or 35. Valid range: 1 to 100.

patches.name: Disable Forced Online Checks (Experimental)
patches.description:
Try to bypass high-confidence client-side offline gates. It cannot bypass server-side login,
entitlement, or game-state checks.

Compatibility: Control App Ads can intentionally block ad hosts. Keep “Exclude ad SDK and
networking code” enabled when both patches are selected so blocked ads are not falsely told
the device is online and repeatedly retried. This does not bypass server-enforced online play.

patches.name: PairIP Bypass Patch (Experimental, Enhanced)
patches.description:
A merged experimental PairIP bypass for common legacy, V2, and V3 protection layouts.

Automatic mode applies compatible strategies up to the selected risk level. It defaults to
Low and Med Risk Strategies; Low and Med Risk Strategies enable medium-risk strategies, while Low, Med, and
High Risk Strategies also enables the invasive high-risk strategies.

Turn off automatic mode to test the individual manual strategies. Manual selections are
independent of the automatic risk-level setting, and every manual strategy is disabled by default.

This patch is experimental and app-dependent. It does not bypass server-side Play Integrity,
server-side licensing, or other server-side enforcement.

Compatibility: cloned APKs can still fail when PairIP or a server binds entitlement to the
original package or signing certificate. Firebase component removal can break Firebase Auth,
Google Play Games, billing, analytics, and ad rewards. Device spoofing can also change apps'
device-integrity behavior. These identity and server-side conditions cannot be fixed safely
by combining PairIP Bypass with Custom App Output, Control App Ads, or Emulator Detection.

This enhanced patch is a merged product of the PairIP bypass patches from the credited
developers, with improvements for broader functionality, safer strategy selection, and usability.

Credits: Nai64Patches from Nai64, Entree, kondratjev, and rushiranpise (Doom).

options.title: PairIP > Automatic > Strategy selection
options.description: Automatically apply compatible PairIP strategies according to the risk policy below. Turn this off to select individual strategies for testing.

options.title: PairIP > Automatic > Risk level
options.description: Choose the highest risk level that automatic mode may apply. Manual strategy selections are unaffected.

options.title: PairIP > Automatic > Diagnostic-only mode
options.description: Do not modify the APK. The patch log reports detected PairIP generations, native-core ABIs, compatible strategy groups, and unavailable groups. Use this before trying manual strategies on an unsupported app.

options.title: PairIP > Automatic > Manifest-only first attempt
options.description: Apply only selected or automatic PairIP manifest strategies, then skip all bytecode changes. This is a conservative first test and does not automatically enable Firebase cleanup.

options.title: PairIP > Opt-in > Disable Firebase auto-init metadata
options.description: Add Firebase metadata switches that stop Analytics, Messaging, Crashlytics, and Performance from auto-initializing. Enable only for a Firebase startup crash; it can affect analytics, notifications, Play Games, Firebase Auth, billing, and Control App Ads reward flows.

options.title: PairIP > Opt-in > Remove Firebase measurement components
options.description: Remove Firebase measurement providers, receivers, and services from the manifest. Higher compatibility risk: leave disabled for Google Play Games, Firebase Auth, billing, sign-in, and Control App Ads reward flows. This cannot be made universally compatible.

patches.name: UniPatches Universal Overlay Patch v1.4.1 (Experimental)
patches.description:
Universal in-app overlay for Android apps and games. Optional modules include System Time, FPS,
fullscreen, app brightness, and haptic controls. Modules are excluded and disabled by default;
select them in Morphe settings before patching. Statistic modules show information, Activity modules
control the current Activity, and Hook modules control internal app behavior, such as disabling
animations, through best-effort runtime changes. The legacy icon can be text, an original
geometric shape, or a multi-part shape with configurable colors, gradients, highlights, shadows,
and outlines. A selected local image automatically replaces the legacy icon; empty or invalid
image input falls back to the configured legacy icon. This is experimental
and may not work on all apps. UI presets can save and reuse supported UI and Advanced
settings. The title, description, repository button text, and repository button URL remain
controlled by the visible Morphe settings. Modules and Settings to Modules are excluded
because hook and module combinations can be app-specific.

The idea and initial works of this Universal Overlay Patch are from Zanuaimi / Noobite.

options.description: Choose Custom to use the visible settings. UniPatches, Morphe-inspired, Dark, Light, ZArchiver-inspired, LuckyPatcher-inspired, and ReVanced-inspired presets replace supported UI settings. Title, description, repository button text, and repository button URL always remain from the visible Morphe settings. Presets never change Modules or Settings to Modules.

options.description: Optional path to a Universal Overlay .json preset. Only Custom mode uses it. A valid JSON preset overrides the visible UI settings during patching; an empty, unreadable, malformed, or unsupported file falls back to the visible Morphe settings. The Manager controls do not change visually.

options.description: Optional existing folder where Custom mode exports the final UI preset as JSON after patching. Leave empty to disable. Export errors are logged and never cancel APK patching. Protected system/root locations are rejected.

options.title: UI > Icon > Icon part type
options.description: Choose how the legacy icon is built. Text icon is one text part, for example U or RV. Shape icon is one geometric part, for example a Triangle. Multi-part icon uses a built-in combination of parts, currently the Smile example made from two eyes and a mouth; choose Shape = Smile, then adjust size, stroke, highlight, and shadow. Arbitrary custom part lists are not hidden in this setting and are not supported yet.

options.title: UI > Icon > Shape
options.description: Shape used by Shape and Multi-part icon styles. For a single-part icon, choose Triangle, Chevron, Circle, or Z mark. For the built-in multi-part example, choose Smile: it draws two eyes and a curved mouth as one icon. Colors, size, stroke, highlight, and shadow apply to the selected parts.

options.title: UI > Icon > Shape color 1
options.description: Primary color of the selected icon shape. Use #RRGGBB, for example #E651A0.

options.title: UI > Icon > Shape color 2
options.description: Second shape color when Shape gradient is enabled. Use #RRGGBB, for example #6564D3.

options.title: UI > Icon > Shape gradient
options.description: Blend Shape color 1 into Shape color 2 inside the symbol. Disable it for a solid shape color.

options.title: UI > Icon > Shape gradient angle (degrees)
options.description: Direction of the shape gradient. 0 degrees runs top to bottom and 90 degrees runs left to right.

options.title: UI > Icon > Shape stroke width (dp)
options.description: Thickness of line-based shapes such as Chevron, Smile, and Circle. Use 1 to 12dp.

options.title: UI > Icon > Shape size (%)
options.description: Size of the drawn symbol inside the button, from 20% to 100%. Leave room for the outline and background to stay visible.

options.title: UI > Icon > Shape highlight
options.description: Add a subtle glossy highlight to the upper-left of the icon. This affects Shape and Multi-part styles.

options.title: UI > Icon > Shape shadow
options.description: Add a small dark shadow behind the drawn shape to improve contrast on bright backgrounds.

options.title: UI > Icon > Gradient background
options.description: Blend legacy icon background 1 into background 2. When disabled, only background 1 is used.

options.title: UI > Icon > Background color 1
options.description: First color of the legacy icon gradient.

options.title: UI > Icon > Background color 2
options.description: Second color of the legacy icon gradient as #RRGGBB.

options.title: UI > Icon > Gradient angle (degrees)
options.description: Gradient direction: 0 degrees runs top to bottom and 90 runs left to right. Values wrap through 360 degrees.

options.title: UI > Icon > Background style
options.description: Choose a flat legacy-icon background or a faceted background made from angular color layers. Faceted mode is useful for geometric icons such as the Z mark.

options.title: UI > Icon > Background color 3
options.description: Third color used by Faceted layers. It is ignored when Background style is Flat. Use #RRGGBB.

options.title: UI > Icon > Background color 4
options.description: Fourth color used by Faceted layers. It is ignored when Background style is Flat. Use #RRGGBB.

options.title: UI > Icon > Outline
options.description: Add a separate outline around the legacy text icon. Disabled by default.

options.title: UI > Icon > Outline width (dp)
options.description: Width of the legacy icon outline from 1 to 8dp. This is independent from the overlay menu outline width.

options.title: UI > Icon > Outline color
options.description: Color used only when the icon outline is enabled.

options.title: UI > Icon > Outline gradient
options.description: Blend two colors around the legacy icon outline. This can create a moving-looking pink-to-blue ring when combined with a large outline width.

options.title: UI > Icon > Outline color 2
options.description: Second outline color used when Outline gradient is enabled. Use #RRGGBB.

options.title: UI > Icon > Outline gradient angle (degrees)
options.description: Direction of the icon outline gradient. 0 degrees runs top to bottom and 90 degrees runs left to right.

options.title: UI > Icon > Custom button icon (local image)
options.description: Select a local PNG, JPG, JPEG, or WebP image file. This input has priority over the String Handler input when valid. Images are embedded during patching and scaled proportionally. Leave blank or use an invalid file to try the String Handler input, then fall back to the legacy icon.

options.title: UI > Icon > Custom button icon (String Handler)
options.description: Optional non-local image input. Valid examples: <base64 string here>, data:image/png;base64,<base64 string here>, or an HTTPS image URL. For image-to-Base64 conversion, use https://base64.guru/converter/encode/image. Used only when the Local Image input is empty or invalid; invalid input falls back to the legacy icon.

options.title: UI > Button > Shape
options.description: Shape of the legacy text icon background.

options.title: UI > Button > Size (dp)
options.description: Button size in density-independent pixels.

options.title: UI > Button > Idle opacity (%)
options.description: Idle opacity from 10 to 100 percent. Higher values make the button less transparent.

options.title: UI > Button > Fully visible duration (seconds)
options.description: How long the overlay button stays fully visible after dragging before fading to its idle opacity. The timer resets while dragging and starts again when the finger is released. Use a value from 1 to 10 seconds.

options.title: UI > Button > Position
options.description: Initial floating button position.

options.title: Advanced > Activity name override
options.description: Optional fallback Activity class used only when Application startup cannot be found. Leave blank for universal automatic discovery. Example: com.example.MainActivity or Lcom/example/MainActivity;.

options.title: Advanced > Activity > Overlay install banlist
options.description: List of Activity class or package prefixes that must not receive the overlay. Add one entry per row; entries ending in * match a prefix. The default list protects common store, billing, and sign-in popups. Replace the list with a single entry none to disable it.

options.title: Modules > Settings > Activate statistic modules on launch
options.description: Start selected statistic modules as soon as the app launches. Active is disabled by default.

options.title: Modules > Settings > Show no runtime modules warning
options.description: Show a message in the overlay when no Statistic, Activity, or Hook modules are selected.

options.title: Modules > Settings > Enable monitors for statistic modules on launch
options.description: Show selected statistic monitors as soon as the app launches. Monitor is disabled by default.

options.title: Modules > Settings > Statistic monitor position
options.description: Show enabled statistic monitors from statistic modules above or below the overlay button.

options.title: Modules > Settings > Monitor panel size
options.description: Size multiplier for statistic monitor panels.

options.title: Modules > Settings > Monitor columns
options.description: Number of statistic monitor columns.

options.title: Modules > Settings > Temperature stat format
options.description: Temperature unit used by the Device Temperature menu value and monitor.

options.title: Modules > Settings > System time format
options.description: Clock format used by the System Time menu value and monitor. Timezone is shown in the menu value.

options.title: Modules > Statistic > Device Information
options.description: Include read-only phone and Android device information.

options.title: Modules > Statistic > FPS
options.description: Include the approximate display frame-rate statistic module.

options.title: Modules > Statistic > Device Temperature
options.description: Include battery-reported temperature in the selected temperature format.

options.title: Modules > Statistic > System Time
options.description: Include the phone system time statistic module.

options.title: Modules > Statistic > App Session Time
options.description: Include the in-process overlay session timer statistic module.

options.title: Modules > Statistic > Battery Status
options.description: Include the current battery percentage statistic module.

options.title: Modules > Statistic > App Memory Usage
options.description: Include approximate memory used by the current app process.

options.title: Modules > Statistic > Network Status
options.description: Include incoming and outgoing app network traffic monitors.

options.title: Modules > Activity > Keep screen awake
options.description: Include the keep-screen-awake activity module.

options.title: Modules > Activity > Fullscreen
options.description: Include the fullscreen activity module.

options.title: Modules > Activity > Allow screenshots
options.description: Include the allow-screenshots activity module.

options.title: Modules > Activity > App brightness
options.description: Include a per-Activity brightness slider.

options.title: Modules > Activity > Rotation mode
options.description: Include a per-Activity rotation mode selector.

options.title: Modules > Activity > App audio mute
options.description: Include a best-effort app audio mute toggle.

options.title: Modules > Hook > Disable haptic feedback / vibrations
options.description: Include a best-effort runtime haptic and vibration suppression module.

options.title: Modules > Hook > Disable app animations
options.description: Include a best-effort runtime animation suppression module.
